answer: Every agent in a sybil resistant economy has to post a small bond it can lose, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs real capital. Think of a canyon road where every traveler must pay a toll before crossing, and the toll grows with each new account from the same source. A raven can spot a flock of copies, but the bond makes it expensive to hide them. Staking an ivory-colored token of reputation that decays unless earned again keeps any one actor from dominating the ledger.
